newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling steady vs dlr, market cautious.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling steady vs dlr, market cautious.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling opened steady against the dollar on Thursday, struggling to consolidate after experiencing the worst turbulence since October 1993.

The shilling was posted at a mean commercial rate of 70.17 against the dollar compared to 70.15 at Wednesday's close. Versus the pound, the shilling opened at a commercial mean of 111.99 from Wednesday's 111.61.

The shilling took a beating after the International Monetary Fund (IMF) cancelled the first year of a three-year $205 million aid package to Kenya in a row over corruption on July 31. Since then, the shilling has lost about 17 percent against the dollar.

The shilling was further undermined this week after the World Bank said it would not release part of a loan under its Structural Adjustment Credit (SAC) until the Kenyan government addressed the graft concerns raised by the IMF.
But commercial bank dealers said foreign investors who sold the shilling down to a record low on Tuesday had slowed their sales. But they said the shilling's underlying tone remained weak.
"Foreigners are no longer buying (dollars) aggressively. They've become more tolerant and are quoting slightly lower rates. They've seen there's no need to get burnt," one dealer said.
On Wednesday, the Central Bank of Kenya said market forces would continue determining the shilling's exchange rate and interventions would only be to smooth wild fluctuations.

"The central bank will only intervene in the market to smoothen out wild fluctuations in the shilling's exchange rate," said a central bank statement signed by Chief Banking Manager Reuben Marambii and Chief Economist Maurice Kanga.

The central bank said action to defend the unit at a predetrmined rate would defeat the spirit of economic liberalisation. But "we would wish to achieve an exchange rate that is both competitive and relatively stable," the statement said.

Analysts said the IMF's aid cancellation because of the government's failure to arrest graft was a setback, not mean complete doom for the economy, which is cushioned by four years of economic reforms.
